messages:
jessica (sec-eng): Quick sync — starting KMS integration for Redwood Private. Need confirmation on envelope flow: control plane should hold CMK references only, data plane stores DEKs encrypted under customer CMK. Thoughts?

arpit (infra): yep that's the plan we've been prototyping. DEKs generated with GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext at write time, store ciphertext_blob with object. Control plane keeps key_id and metadata only.

maria (platform): one big callout: DEK cache TTL on runtime instances. If we cache DEKs, we need eviction on key rotation + rewrap. What's our intended TTL?

jessica (sec-eng): thinking default 15m, configurable per deployment. Also need a rewrap pipeline for rotation that: 1) generates new DEKs via CMK, 2) re-encrypts persisted objects (async), 3) marks old DEKs retired.

lina (prod-sre): for incidents we need immediate rollback options. If a CMK is suspected compromised, runbook should: disable CMK, revoke active grants, rotate DEKs with new CMK, and fail closed for read-after-write depending on SLA.

arpit (infra): regarding grants — we'll create per-service grants with conditions (encryptionContext) and duration 1h, auto-renewable via role. Use CreateGrant so we can revoke quickly. Note: KMS grants are cross-account-friendly if CMK is in cust account.

jessica (sec-eng): agree. Also ensure IAM roles used by control plane have kms:ReEncrypt*, kms:GenerateDataKey* and kms:CreateGrant permissions only when needed. Map RBAC: platform-service -> role that maps to service account.

maria (platform): audit logging: CloudTrail will show KMS API calls, but we should also emit higher-level events from control plane: key_id, operation (wrap/unwrap/rewrap), object_id fingerprint. Those need to be JSON logs ingested into our audit index.

lina (prod-sre): add retention policy for audit logs — 7 years for enterprise customers. Also preserve rewrap job traces so we can correlate objects re-encrypted during a rotation.

arpit (infra): networking: KMS through VPC endpoint only for Private. Ensure endpoint policy allows kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:ReEncryptFrom. We might front with a lightweight KMS proxy inside the VPC that enforces RBAC and returns grant tokens. Proxy helps in multi-cloud (GCP/Azure) abstraction later.

jessica (sec-eng): KMS proxy idea sounds useful. It should sign requests with short-lived credentials and attach an internal auth header. Keep audit of proxied calls. Avoid proxy being single point of failure — run 3 replicas across AZs.

maria (platform): rotation workflow detail: for scheduled rotation, orchestrator picks batch of object prefixes, calls ReEncrypt (ReEncryptFrom) to produce new ciphertext, atomically swap pointer, and then mark old ciphertext for garbage collection. Need idempotency keys.

arpit (infra): we'll implement background rewrap with idempotency: job id, object list snapshot, status stream. If job fails, it retries from last acknowledged object. Add metrics for rewrap throughput and error-rate.

jessica (sec-eng): incident playbook stub:
```
- detect: CloudTrail KMS anomalies or CMK policy change alert
- contain: disable CMK, revoke grants, notify oncall
- eradicate: create new CMK, kick-off rewrap job, rotate service credentials
- recover: validate re-encryption, enable keys, update audit
- review: postmortem and key access audit
```

lina (prod-sre): oncall rotation: if key compromise happens overnight, oncall should trigger rewrap job and escalate to infra. We need a CLI runbook command: `redwood kms incident start --cmk <old> --new-cmk <new>` that automates steps.

samir (oncall-bot): reminder set: weekly smoke test for rewrap pipeline every Friday 03:00 UTC.

maria (platform): tests: unit for GenerateDataKey usage, integration test with real KMS via test account, and a canary rewrap run on a 100-object bucket with deploy-bot ensuring zero-downtime.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled to eng-private on 1899992100, will run rewrap-job-canary after deploy.

arpit (infra): extra security nit: use encryption context with service and object_id to prevent ciphertext substitution. Also consider storing a short SHA256(DEK_plain) fingerprint in HSM-backed metadata (never the DEK itself) to detect tampering.

jessica (sec-eng): final open questions: 1) who manages CMKs for customers in marketplace vs BYOK? 2) KMS proxy auth model (signed JWT vs assume-role) — opinions?

maria (platform): for BYOK, prefer customer-managed CMK in their account with cross-account grants. For marketplace-managed, Redwood creates a CMK in a dedicated account and offers ledgering. Proxy auth: signed JWT issued by control plane STS is my pick.

lina (prod-sre): I'll draft the CLI runbook and incident playbook tomorrow. arpit — can you sketch the proxy PoC this week?

arpit (infra): yes, I'll spin up proxy PoC and endpoint policy diff. Posting links when ready.

jessica (sec-eng): perfect — thanks all. We'll converge on RBAC mappings and the audit schema in follow-up thread. :thumbsup:
